Hi useRs,

I am new here. Here is my question.

I am trying to do Latent curve model in R. But all the examples I found are not very helpful. They are all about four time point. Why is that? 
I have longitudinal data of three month.  I can just code 1*t1+2*t2+3*t3.......90*t90 into R studio, right?

This paper 'Latent Growth Modeling for Information Systems: Theoretical Extensions and Practical Applications' used the model. I cannot use the same model even I have read the four-time-point examples hundred times.

Thank you.

Qingyuan

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: A question about growth() in Lavaan
parts: They are all about four time point. Why is that?
Because the same principles apply to growth across 4 time points as across 90.  It's just an easier example to work with 4 than 90.
I have longitudinal data of three month.  I can just code 1*t1+2*t2+3*t3.......90*t90 into R studio, right?

This paper 'Latent Growth Modeling for Information Systems: Theoretical Extensions and Practical Applications' used the model. I cannot use the same model even I have read the four-time-point examples hundred times.

Try reading the 26-time-point example on p. 22 (see Figure 3).  It appears in this paper that they only fixed the first and last loadings for the Slope factor to 0 and 1, and estimated the rest (i.e., a latent basis growth curve; see Table 5), but that is not necessary if you want to fit a specific functional form of growth/decline.

Terry
